segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, thanks for making time, Karen. I pulled up the order form draft. We have 42 seats, annual term starting July 15, and the services package for the initial setup. Does that line up with what you were expecting?

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Yes, mostly. We may need 45 seats instead of 42. Finance added three managers who want dashboard access, but they won’t be heavy users.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Got it. For 45 seats, the subscription moves from $38,640 to $41,400 for the year. Same per-seat rate, no change to the services line. I can update that in the CRM after this call.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Okay. And the services piece is still $6,500, right? That includes the two training sessions?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Correct. $6,500 flat. That covers the kickoff, configuration support, and two 90-minute trainings. If you want a third session later, it would be quoted separately, but most teams your size are fine with two.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: That should be fine. On invoicing, can you split it so the subscription is due at signature and the services are billed on August 1? Our implementation budget opens then.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, we can do that. I’ll note subscription invoiced on signature, services invoiced August 1 with net 30 terms. Legal usually approves that without an issue.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Great. We’re targeting go-live on September 9. Is that realistic if we sign by July 12?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yes. If signature is in by July 12, we can schedule kickoff the week of July 22. That gives us about seven weeks, which is comfortable for your data volume and the three workflows you outlined.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Okay. Send the revised order form with 45 seats and the split invoicing language. I’ll route it to procurement today.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Will do. I’ll send it by 2:00 p.m. Central. I’ll also include the implementation summary so procurement has the scope in one place.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Perfect. If they have questions on the payment terms, I’ll loop you in. Thanks.
